bilingual.notes: Maryland's COMAR 13A.12.02 certification chapter has no separate bilingual-education credential track (no DBE/DLBE/TBE). EL instruction is delivered via the ESOL credential.

eld.notes: ESOL Pre-K-12 (COMAR 13A.12.02.19). Approved program with 54 sem hrs of required coursework, 6 sh supervised ESOL student teaching (or 1 yr ESOL teaching experience), Praxis 5362, and 6 sh in a modern foreign language at the college level for the teacher candidate. The teacher-candidate language requirement is unusual nationally.

history.title: Maryland adopts State Seal of Biliteracy (SB 781, Ch. 232, 2016)
history.description: SB 781 (Chapter 232, 2016) authorized the Maryland State Seal of Biliteracy, codified at Education Article §7-208. MSDE administers the credential for high-school graduates proficient in English plus one or more world languages; participation is district-opt-in.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Maryland's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

elPercentHistory.note: Maryland Department of Education, September 30 fall snapshot (112,081 EL students). Maryland publishes a multi-year EL series whose fall 2020 and fall 2021 figures match NCES Digest Table 204.20 within 0.01 percentage points (MDE 88,834 / NCES 10.1% and MDE 98,566 / NCES 11.2%), so the Maryland series can be treated as methodologically continuous with the prior NCES series. The 1.4 percentage-point increase over NCES's fall 2021 value (11.2%) tracks the documented upward trajectory through 2023-24.
